limitations: Failed per-run gates are retained in the JSON and excluded from comparison rows and metric leaders. All results are cross-allocation and prescribed endpoint observations (40 steps for one node; 80 for two), not a controlled matched-work strong-scaling or stable speedup claim.
New-job PBS resource MPI process requests differ from allocated CPU counts; CPU cost and whole-allocation utilization use allocated ncpus, while partition and solver checks use actual MPI ranks.
Current retained scripts are sealed collection evidence but are not proof of the frozen bytes submitted to PBS; owner and submit provenance remain unverified.
PBS F/exit0 and native End do not establish each native command returned zero: the common helper accepts End and can mask a nonzero command status.

Processor fields, mesh binaries/independent mesh identity, final zero-field seals, environment state, per-rank affinity/physical-core map, hardware telemetry, and posted charge were not collected. exec_host identifies allocated hosts only.

Estimated SU is elapsed walltime × allocated CPUs × queue charge rate / 3600, not a posted/reconciled charge. cpupercent is PBS last sample; derived whole-allocation CPU use is CPUT/(walltime × ncpus).

Native minimum sample recommendations and any emitted short-sample warning are recorded per run. These diagnostics are not formal independent confidence intervals; preserve the prescribed ranked endpoints and per-step variation. No causal bottleneck is inferred.

Partial preparation timer sum combines decomposePar algorithm duration with renumberMesh, potentialFoam, and applyBoundaryLayer ClockTime values. It excludes decomposePar processor-mesh/field transfer and write, read/I/O, and unattributed time, so it is not a full setup/init measure or a setup winner.
Negative omega bounding minima are diagnostics also present in accepted controls; no fields or counters diagnose their cause.
